primary_claim: Standard mechanistic interpretability techniques (logit lens, activation patching, probing) can reveal that a CODI latent-reasoning model stores intermediate math calculation results in specific latent vectors (the third and fifth of six)

effect.metric: accuracy recovery / answer-flip rate under activation patching
effect.value: model recovers ~20% accuracy (from 55% baseline) when patching in latent vectors after mean-ablating specific numbers; patching third/fifth latent vectors with different-intermediate-value vectors notably decreases accuracy while same-value patching leaves accuracy unchanged

contradicts_or_qualifies: Original CODI paper's No-CoT-SFT baseline comparison, which the authors argue is confounded by training data differences
stated_future_work: Investigate whether interpretable structures can be found in messier in-the-wild prompts where intermediate steps are ambiguous or reasoning requires abstract, non-numerical steps
Stress-test and prepare interpretability techniques for latent reasoning models in case they become standard
limitations_stated: Study performed on a small model trained only to solve math tasks; unclear how results hold up at larger scale and more complex tasks
Experiments relied on math templates with fixed structure requiring exactly two intermediate steps
Model co-trained on verbalized CoT may have a natural-language prior instilled that models trained via pure RL without a verbalized teacher may not have, making them potentially less interpretable
This was a time-boxed research sprint and the authors decided not to pursue this direction further
quote: We find that the model solves maths problems requiring three reasoning steps by storing the two intermediate values in specific latent vectors (the third and fifth of six).
